## Security verdict: BLOCK

PR #215 at **4b719a4f9446fc847e180905b0b15019a0851eb9**, under C33/C34. These are normal-use configuration-integrity and state-reporting defects, not same-user impersonation findings. PM confirmed both block against Jordan's explicit restore and reporting rules.

| # | Severity | File | Lines | Vulnerability | Confidence |
|---|----------|------|-------|---------------|------------|
| S215-001 | 🟡 MEDIUM | `crates/harnesses/src/claude_settings.rs`; `crates/daemon/src/http/revive.rs` | 1190-1272; 550-599 | Global-settings restoration is neither byte-exact nor fail-closed | 10/10 |
| S215-002 | 🟡 MEDIUM | `crates/daemon/src/cheap_return.rs` | 159-186 | Recorded model is changed without establishing that the in-session switch applied | 10/10 |

### S215-001: global settings can remain changed after an apparently successful operation

The snapshot retains parsed model values, not the original bytes (`claude_settings.rs:1190-1201`). An absent original model is removed by reserializing the whole object (`1208-1237`), so unrelated formatting/key-order bytes change. Missing, unreadable, invalid or non-object settings are omitted from the snapshot rather than refusing the switch. Restoration can therefore lack the state required to undo a model change; an unparsable restore document can produce no edit without an explicit parse-error report.

The existing temporary-file/write/sync/rename helper makes each replacement atomic (`1049-1075`), but that is not failure-safe restoration of the whole operation. Restore errors after launch are stderr-only and do not replace the revive response (`revive.rs:550-599`). A successful or ordinary failed launch is not proof that the global default was restored. The `--ask` nonwaiting path also does not synchronize restoration with completion of startup writes.

Required repair: preserve the exact required original state, refuse before switching when it cannot be saved, handle absent-file/absent-model cases explicitly, and make restoration failure an observable failed operation with recovery information. Do not silently skip a governed settings file or claim byte identity after whole-object reserialization. Only intended `settings.json` paths may be touched; no real user config was read in this review.

### S215-002: a late or absent dialog can leave boundModel wrong

After `/model` submission, a successful pane capture without `Switch model?` yields `confirmed=false`, but the recorded model update still runs (`cheap_return.rs:159-186`). No observed-model evidence distinguishes an immediate no-dialog success from the documented late-dialog case in which the switch has not applied. Thus the known failure can still publish the requested return model as the actual model, making seat/model reporting incorrect.

Required repair: update the recorded model only on evidence the switch applied; otherwise retain the last established model and report the incomplete return explicitly. Do not equate “input was submitted” with “model changed.”

### Explicit notes, not additional blocks

**S215-N001: selector validation.** The recorded model is interpolated into `/model` without a model-selector grammar check before typing (`revive.rs:357-370`; `cheap_return.rs:150`). Bracketed paste and the adapter's control checks are not selector validation; newline is not rejected by that control filter. No shell-injection exploit or hostile same-user finding is asserted.

**S215-N002: Enter provenance.** The code does read the pane after its own successful gated submission, and capture failure sends no Enter. However, the check is a substring anywhere in 40 captured lines, not proof of an active matching dialog or its selected action; `press_enter` is outside the input-submission ownership transaction (`cheap_return.rs:148-165`; `crates/tmux/src/lib.rs:1066-1069`). No concrete unauthorized-confirmation exploit was established. Keep this limitation explicit.

The target filename is fixed. Homes are discovered from `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` or the normal Claude home plus the alternate home; the model supplies no file path. Replacement writes are individually atomic. These positive properties do not close S215-001.

**CI proof:** clean detached worktree HEAD and GitHub/remote heads agree; GitHub reports CLEAN and all five checks successful. Run [42750463077](https://github.com/AI-Substrate/pij-fleet/actions/runs/42750463077) checked merge `d1940eade8ef263cff91847adc1f47b113a6846c`, whose parents are base `04c9e107b2f73497b4142c361bc1e6e0f5d28401` and this exact head. Rust reports **2,371 passed, 6 skipped**. Successful artifact `13733790504` includes both cheap-return tests, the model-restore test and 19 revive HTTP cases. Passing happy-path/fake tests do not establish the failure guarantees above.

Static source review and existing CI only. No local builds/tests, real user-settings/credential reads, live pane inspection/typing, product mutations or exploit probes.
